relationships.rationale: Proving value end-to-end within 90 days depends on a single team owning the solution from design through operation, without handovers.
An MVP that proves value end-to-end must still be operable, observable, and secure — production readiness cannot be deferred to a later phase.
This strategy is the direct mandate for solution architects to search the existing pattern catalogue before commissioning anything bespoke.
This strategy is the direct mandate for operability, observability, and security being designed into the solution from the start.
No initiative passing its first release gate without operability sign-off depends on every service having a published SLO as part of that sign-off.
Five-year operate-and-exit costs being reviewed by Finance and Architecture jointly is enacted through the Architecture Council review gate for cross-domain solutions.
Investment cases that include operate and exit costs depend on production readiness — including its ongoing operating cost — being designed in from the start, not bolted on later.
A documented evolution and exit plan for every solution is reviewed through the same Architecture Council gate that governs cross-domain solutions.
A credible exit path depends on the decisions and constraints that shaped the original design being recorded as ADRs, so future teams can re-evaluate them as constraints evolve.

activity.notes: Reviewed and refined during the 2026-Q1 architecture cycle.
